sources.head_base: The head model is a rigid shell whose neck stub flares at its base: the ring on the neck joint plane is 65 mm wide each side and 41 to 66 mm deep, the rows above it 46 to 51 mm. Turned with the head it swings those lobes out of the skin's neck, which takes only part of the turn, and over the collar beside the shoulder. With the skinned body drawn, shell vertices below height_m above the neck joint plane are held inside an ellipse round the neck axis (half width side_m, depth front_m forward and back_m behind) and drawn down the neck by drop_m at the joint plane, falling to nothing at height_m. A first version held them in a 30 mm circle. Measured 2026-11-20 on the default subject at the address, top, impact and finish poses with the head turned 1.4 rad either way: 9.2 to 17.5 mm outside the skin with no hold, 3.7 mm or more inside with the circle, 2.2 mm or more inside now. The circle opened the join under the jaw: the skin's neck rim stands 79 mm forward of the axis, the stub's front wall 62 mm (17 mm apart) and the circle 30 mm (49 mm apart), and the stub ends level with the rim, so a view from the front passed between them and out through the back of the neck. See-through pixels round the neck of a tour-average subject over a fitted driver swing (55 frames, four cameras, 480 px square, 0.6 m away): no hold 7,784, the circle 22,299, now 10,810; an ellipse 50 mm sideways with the front wall kept and drawn 10 % forward gave 5,844 but stands 12.3 mm outside the skin at the 1.4 rad turn. What the turn check leaves room for, to the millimetre and with 1 mm to spare: 48 to 55 mm forward, 31 to 34 mm sideways, 30 to 46 mm behind; front 0.052 came 1.5 mm outside, and a side or back wider than 30 mm changed the pixel count by under 1 %. Drop 0.010 gave 11,357, 0.015 10,251; 0.018 puts the base beside a fold of skin under the neck at the top pose (40 mm outside by the check). The slit behind the jaw seen face-on (501 pixels in the worst frame) is at the side, where a rigid base has no room, and stays. With the skin's neck end drawn in and closed by a plug (dress_settings.json, neck_cap; same day) the neck is 14 mm narrower under the jaw: front 0.05 then stood 1.2 and 2.5 mm outside the skin at the 1.4 rad turn (top and finish poses), 0.044 0.1 and 0.6 mm inside, front_m 0.042 1.0 and 1.7 mm inside, 0.040 3.8 and 4.5 mm; the plug closes the view through the neck, so the front wall no longer has to stand as far forward. Jaw line (2026-11-20): above height_m the shell's neck stub is the skin's neck drawn a second time, 2 to 5 mm from it, so the two cut each other in a ragged line under the jaw and behind the ear and are lit apart. The hold onto the ellipse therefore goes on up to the plane jaw_height_m (60 mm) above the joint on the neck axis, dropping jaw_slope (0.5) per metre forward so that it passes under the jaw, and lets go over flare_m (12 mm) below that plane; flare_m 0 with jaw_height_m 0 holds the base only. A stub held that high must be narrower than the base alone to stay in the neck at the 1.4 rad turn, and the neck's end is drawn 20 mm in for it (neck_cap tuck_m). Default subject, largest distance outside the skin of a stub vertex (between height_m and 12 mm under the jaw line) at head turns 0 / 0.7 / 1.4 rad: -3.7 / 4.5 / 15.5 mm with no hold above the base; 7.5 mm at 1.4 rad with the base's 42 / 30 / 30 mm ellipse; -14.6 / -8.6 / -0.7 mm at 34 / 24 / 24 mm; -15.3 / -9.2 / -2.6 mm at front_m 0.036, side_m and back_m 0.022, the values kept (the base itself then 11.3 mm or more inside). A 22 mm circle with no drop, the first form of the jaw-line hold, measures the same at the stub but covers the rim less (head_join_limits: 31.9 to 49.1 / 19.5 against 50.2 to 64.2 / 40.4). Border between head model and neck skin drawn over a fitted driver swing of a tour-average subject (55 frames, four cameras, 480 px square, 0.6 m away; pixels of border / separate patches at it): base hold only 43,324 / 823, with the jaw-line hold 35,621 / 623. The loft body keeps the whole shell.
sources.head_base_limits: Check of head_base: with the head turned turn_rad either way at the top and finish poses of tests/fixtures/model_appearance/swing_poses.json, no head shell vertex below below_m above the neck joint plane may lie more than outside_m outside the posed skin (signed distance along the nearest skin vertex's normal). 1.4 rad is the head's turn against the chest at the top of a fitted driver swing (1.15 rad at its finish). jaw_below_m: the same check, also with the head straight and at the address pose, for every shell vertex between below_m and jaw_below_m (12 mm, the flare) under the jaw line of head_base.
sources.head_join_limits: Check of head_base at the address, top, impact and finish poses of tests/fixtures/model_appearance/swing_poses.json. For each vertex of the skin's neck rim within sector_deg of straight ahead (head frame), the cover angle is the steepest dip below level at which a sight line over that vertex towards the neck axis still meets the head shell, taking shell points within window_deg of the vertex's direction; a steeper line passes under the shell's base into the open neck. Its mean over the front of the rim may not be under mean_cover_deg, nor any vertex under least_cover_deg. Measured 2026-11-20 (mean / least, degrees): no hold 31.9 to 45.4 / -0.7; the 30 mm circle 13.9 to 28.1 / -0.5; the ellipse with no drop 20.4 to 34.1 / -0.6; the ellipse with front 0.05 37.0 to 49.3 / 21.3. The rim is the end of the skin's own neck; the plug that closes it (dress_settings.json, neck_cap) is left out of the check, which so reads the join the plug hides. With the end drawn in under the jaw and front_m 0.042: 52.0 to 63.2 / 37.5; with the jaw-line hold (front_m 0.036, neck_cap tuck_m 20 mm): 50.2 to 64.2 / 40.4. The mean bound is the unheld shell's own cover, rounded down; the least bound asks for the drop, without which the base ends level with the rim.
sources.wrist_blend: A skinned hand is drawn rigid on the club, so a forearm that follows only its own body leaves the hand's cuff at a bent wrist. Over the last wrist_blend_length_m (35 mm) before the wrist joint the forearm's skin passes smoothly (smoothstep) to the body the hand moves with, and is whole on it from wrist_blend_full_m (12 mm) before the joint: the skin's end ring, 10 to 12 mm before the joint. The row behind it, 14 to 20 mm before the joint, is 0.72 to 0.98 the hand's. The blend is linear between two rigid bodies, so skin shared half and half is drawn in by the cosine of half the hand's turn against the forearm, whether that turn is a bend or a twist about the forearm; in a fitted driver swing the turn reaches 100 degrees (up to 98 of bend with 25 to 60 of twist). The first length, 70 mm, shared two rows of the skin (30 and 52 mm before the joint) and wrung the forearm to a third of its depth there. 35 mm leaves the row at 52 mm with the forearm and gives the row at 28 to 36 mm at most 0.22 to the hand, so the forearm keeps its section up to the hand and tapers into the cuff. Measured 2026-11-20 over a fitted driver swing (showpiece profile, tenth-percentile depth 20 to 90 mm before the joint against rest, worst frame): 0.29 lead and 0.18 trail at 70 mm, 0.77 and 0.77 at 35 mm; 30 and 25 mm measure higher still but leave a step and a thin stem behind the cuff. Whole from 15 mm (with 35 mm) the row behind the end ring is rigid with the hand and folds 20 to 21 faces of the skin at a wrist bent 30 degrees, over swing_limits.folded_share; whole from 12 mm folds 2 to 13, as the 70 mm blend did (2 to 12). A share of the twist cannot be given to the skin further up: the model has no body that turns part of the way, a MuJoCo skin bone must be a body, and a body that follows a share of the hand's turn needs a joint or a pose set from outside each frame; a per-vertex offset on extra bones of the two bodies is exact at one turn only and off by 15 mm 40 degrees away from it. A length of 0 switches the blend off and leaves the bones as they were. Only with the skinned hands on a club.
sources.wrist_limits: Checks of the blend with a wrist bent bend_deg (30 degrees) each way in flexion and deviation. end_shift_m: the forearm's end may move this far against its hand's body; measured 0 (it is rigid with it), against 16.1 mm with the blend off; 0.2 mm is a tenth of the 2 mm the skin lies under the hand's wrist section (fit_settings.json, wrist_under_m). end_to_hand_m: largest distance from the forearm's end ring (the vertices whole on the hand) to the hand's surface in the MuJoCo model; measured 8.7 to 8.8 mm at every bend (it ends 8 mm behind the hand's rim and lies 2 mm inside it; 11.6 mm with the row behind it, which was whole on the hand until the blend was shortened), against 16 to 29 mm for the end ring with the blend off (2026-11-20, default subject, wrist joints on the skinned hands'). depth_band_m, thin_share, depth_ratio: at the wrist coordinates of skinned_hand_wrists in tests/fixtures/model_appearance/swing_poses.json (hands turned 62 to 100 degrees against the forearms) at most thin_share of the forearm's skin vertices between the two distances of depth_band_m before the wrist joint may have less than depth_ratio of their rest depth (body_skin_mesh.inward_thickness). Measured on the default subject, lead and trail: 0.53 to 0.60 and 0.36 to 0.43 with the 70 mm blend, 0.72 to 0.75 and 0.71 to 0.72 with 35 mm whole from 12 mm; the hand's own wrist section is narrower than the forearm 30 mm behind it, so the depth cannot stay whole in the band. join_past_m, join_step_m (2026-11-20): at the address and at those swing wrists no part of a drawn hand may reach more than join_past_m past the plane of the forearm's end ring up the arm, the hand must reach to within join_past_m of that plane, and round the ring the hand's rim may differ from the ring by at most join_step_m in radius about the ring's centre. Measured on a fitted tour-average subject: 12.0 to 13.8 mm past and 3.2 to 3.7 mm proud with the hand's wrist ball (its own skin ending 8 mm short), 5.1 mm past and +0.1 to +1.6 mm proud with the sleeve (hand_visual_quality.json, forearm_wrist_shape.sleeve).
sources.swing_limits: Bounds on the drawn surface at the swing-like poses of tests/fixtures/model_appearance/swing_poses.json, against the bind pose: the share of a layer's faces whose area changes by more than area_ratio either way, and the share turned against the surface around them. Measured 2026-11-20 on the default and the showpiece profile: at most 4.97 % stretched (shirt at the top, under the arms) and 0.52 % folded (shirt, 0.45 % of it at address already, on the garment hems). The bounds hold the present state with margin for another subject; they are not a quality target: single faces at the trouser hip crease and under the arm change area up to 26 times.
sources.covered_parts: Body parts (model_appearance.library classes) whose loft meshes the skin replaces; hands, head, feet and club keep their own models, and the head model's neck is left out because the skin has one.
sources.spine_follow: Share of the thorax's motion relative to the pelvis taken by the spine05, spine04 and spine03 group (the rest stays with the pelvis). 0.1, 0.45 and 0.8 are the #15299 prototype's values: the waistband stays on the pelvis and the lower ribs turn with the chest.
sources.weight_floor: A body share under 0.0001 of a vertex is dropped and the rest renormalised; it moves a vertex less than 0.1 mm per metre of relative body motion and keeps the bone lists short.
sources.bind_pose: Model coordinates (radians; every other coordinate zero) of the pose the bones are bound in: both arms hanging at the side, the closest model pose to the stored skin's rest pose, so the turn from one to the other is small and carries almost no twist about a bone.
sources.bind_stretch_limit_m: Largest change of an edge length allowed between the fitted rest pose and the bind pose. Measured 20.9 mm (2026-11-20) with the body origins of the 1.71 m default subject in tests/unit/model_appearance/test_body_skin_export.py, at the shoulder where the arm comes down from the stored rest pose; the bound leaves margin for a subject of another size.
